analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES - More pain in semis; Amadeus solid; Rightmove trims guide, Cellnex solid; Cloudflare beat & raise
key_insights: US equities sold off sharply on 11/5: Nasdaq 100 -6.36%, S&P 500 -4.36%, SOX -12%. Post-election concerns over tighter AI regulation and data-centre permitting added pressure to an already fragile trade and prompted investors to reassess the 2028+ capex outlook.

Selling spread across AI infrastructure, power and neoclouds, with little defensive support from hyperscalers. ETF-led de-risking and heavy demand for protection dominated, and buyers stayed reluctant to step in. Little relief so far in Asia.

Lam Research announced a $25bn share repurchase programme, about 10% of its market cap. The desk would not be surprised to see similar announcements across semiconductors in the coming days and weeks.

Desk activity: Wednesday was one of the busiest days of the year on the equities desk, while Thursday was the opposite. Inbound requests for color were 10/10 but overall activity was 5/10. The desk reads price action as top-down pressure through macro instruments, with massive notionals traded across the ETF complex.

Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa said currently permitted data-centre projects will be allowed to complete construction, which the desk says covers all of 2027 and likely well into 2028. She plans laws requiring newly permitted data centres to pay taxes, commit to no rise in consumer power prices and avoid affecting residential water availability. The desk calls this more reasonable than the headlines suggest.

PB desk data: global fundamental long/short managers fell 1.3% (a -2 standard-deviation move), mainly from market/beta exposure, leaving YTD at +8.7%. TMT funds fell more than 4% and are roughly flat to slightly positive YTD, down from about +24% before the June/July AI sell-off.
Many GS AI-related baskets had their biggest down day since the launch of ChatGPT.

Credit: after the Democratic midterm sweep, the most leveraged AI infrastructure names are hit and their bonds are distressed, with CDS implying a >60% 5Y default probability (GS credit strategist Amanda Lynam).

Hyperscalers are using credit access as a competitive advantage. They raised $67bn across five deals since late October, taking YTD issuance to $296bn. That funds 36% of 2026 capex and exceeds the $250bn full-year forecast. Pulling 2027 borrowing forward raises the risk of further credit-spread widening through early December.

GS 2027 projection: $440bn of direct hyperscaler debt covering 35% of capex, plus $300bn of investment-grade/high-yield project finance. Regional data-centre moratoriums threaten about 45% of planned US expansion, mainly in Texas. Projects with secured grid access should price tight, while speculative projects without power could face wider spreads, stricter covenants or delays.

Rightmove cut FY26 revenue growth guidance to 6-7% from 6-8% on weaker new homes. ARPA growth is now £100-110 versus £110-120. Adjusted operating profit growth is at least 3% (was 3-5%) and underlying EPS growth at least 7% (was at least 5%), slightly below consensus of 7.6%.

Rightmove FY27 guidance implies modest revenue and EPS downgrades: revenue growth similar to FY26 (consensus 7.5%), EPS growth of at least 10% (consensus 10.8%), margins of at least 67%. Planned shareholder returns remain above £400m by 31 July 2027, including about £330m of buybacks.

Amadeus Q3 was in line, with FCF better than consensus (EUR564.2mn vs EUR532.6mn) and guidance reiterated at the lower end because of the Middle East situation. Operating income was EUR506.7mn vs consensus EUR521.7mn. The desk says the Street (4.6%) is already at the low end.

Cellnex delivered an in-line 3Q26 with guidance reiterated. A value-accretive Poland deal and cost efficiencies lifted EBITDA margin, but management warned the margin gain may not be sustainable and PoP growth stayed historically low. Structural concerns (telco consolidation, satellite competition, contract renegotiation) limit near-term rerating.

Microchip had a solid quarter in line on revenue, margins and EPS, but FY3Q guidance came in below GIR and Street forecasts, so the stock is likely to trade lower. GS sees limited read-across to analog peers because most have already reported.

Cloudflare (NET) beat and raised, with shares indicated up 14-18%. Q3 revenue rose 39.2% to $782.5m and Q4 guidance of $845-846m beat Street by about 6%. Current RPO growth accelerated to 37%. Gross margin fell 287bps y/y to 72.4%, 84bps below Street, operating margin met expectations at 17.5%, and FCF margin fell to 10.5% from 13.3%.

Atlassian (TEAM) fell 20%. Q1 cloud revenue grew 30.5% to $1.30bn, its first slowdown in six quarters, and Q2 cloud growth guidance of about 27% was below investor expectations of 28-28.5%. The FY27 upgrade to 26% only reflected the Q1 beat, implying 2H growth of 23.6% vs Street 24%.
Away from GS: Nemetschek's call left reduced visibility in Design, with no clear Q4 steer. GIR is at about 8% growth, similar to the Street, and sees the Street possibly moving lower.

Away from GS: DIGITIMES reports consumer NAND procurement has largely frozen after about 18 months of price increases. October US-supplier quotes were flat and 512Gb TLC wafer spot prices fell about 6.5%. DRAM may still rise in 4Q26 at a slower pace, making 4Q26-1Q27 a critical inventory and pricing test.

Away from GS: Taiwan supply-chain sources say AI-server demand remains strong and shipment volatility reflects Nvidia platform transitions, not cancellations. DIGITIMES infers the correction is driven more by financing, regulation and valuation worries than by verified supply cuts.

Amazon is offering US Prime members free Uber Eats delivery on orders of $25 or more, a week after DoorDash's $17bn Instacart deal. DoorDash fell more than 15% to $168.32 and Rosenblatt cut its DoorDash target to $225 from $270.

Desk flows: asset managers were net sellers on steady supply across semis and AI, and there was no offsetting bid for hyperscalers and defensive tech as there was the day before. Hedge fund flows were about balanced while shorts were toggled aggressively.

Derivatives: vol exploded with hedge monetization dominating early flows in S&P, Nasdaq and VIX. The GS Vol Panic Index hit 9.3 out of 10. The implied move through the next day is 1.43%. Futures closed below the medium-term CTA threshold (7549), with an estimated $7.48bn of S&P selling over the next week in a -2.5 stdev scenario.

Telco call takeaways: BT's call was more bullish on consumer than earlier IR comments, with consumer EBITDA broadly flat for FY versus -1.5% in H1. Swisscom sounded cautious on further price rises given higher churn. Bouygues confirmed its deal is on track and Equans beat and raised guidance.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 revenue +39.2% to $782.5m and Q4 guide beat Street by about 6%, with shares indicated up 14-18%. Gross margin missed Street by 84bps.
Shares fell 20% as cloud growth slowed to 30.5% and Q2 cloud guidance of about 27% missed investor expectations of 28-28.5%.
FY3Q guidance came in below GIR and Street, so the stock is likely to trade lower despite an in-line quarter.
Announced a $25bn buyback, about 10% of market cap. The desk expects similar announcements across semis.
Rosenblatt cut its target to $225 from $270 after Amazon's free Uber Eats offer for Prime members. The stock fell more than 15% to $168.32.
Fell more than 4% in the broader tech sell-off after launching the Uber Eats Prime offer.
Fell more than 2% as Amazon's Prime tie-up raises questions for Uber One membership.

sector_views.rationale: SOX multiples have compressed about 50% from the June/July highs. Bottom-up demand indicators are still firm, but investors want signs of stabilisation. The open debate is whether delays to AI infrastructure spending are already priced in.
Cellnex's structural concerns (telco consolidation, satellite competition, contract renegotiation) limit near-term rerating despite the Poland deal.

earnings_insights: Cloudflare (NET) Q3 reported: revenue $782.5m, +39.2% y/y. Q4 guidance $845-846m, about 6% above Street. Gross margin 72.4% (-287bps y/y, 84bps below Street), operating margin 17.5% (in line with Street), FCF margin 10.5% vs 13.3% a year earlier. Current RPO growth 37%.

Atlassian (TEAM) Q1 reported: cloud revenue $1.30bn, +30.5% y/y. Total revenue $1.77bn, in line with investor expectations. Q2 cloud growth guide about 27% vs investor expectations of 28-28.5%. FY27 cloud growth guide 26%, implying 2H growth of 23.6% vs Street 24%. Full-year operating margin guide 25.5% beat Street, but implied 2H operating profit is about $79m below consensus.

Amadeus Q3 reported: revenue EUR1.74bn vs consensus EUR1.74bn, EBITDA EUR694.1mn vs consensus EUR694.4mn, operating income EUR506.7mn vs consensus EUR521.7mn, FCF EUR564.2mn vs consensus EUR532.6mn, bookings EUR121.2mn vs consensus EUR121.8mn. FY guidance on track but at the lower end.

Rightmove FY26 guidance (company guide, not a print): revenue growth 6-7% (was 6-8%), adjusted operating profit growth at least 3% (was 3-5%), underlying EPS growth at least 7% (was at least 5%) vs consensus 7.6%. FY27 guide: EPS growth at least 10% vs consensus 10.8%, revenue growth similar to FY26 vs consensus 7.5%.
Cellnex 3Q26 reported in line with guidance reiterated. EBITDA margin expanded on cost efficiencies, but management cautioned it may not be sustainable.
Microchip reported a quarter in line on revenue, margins and EPS. FY3Q guidance was below both GIR and Street forecasts.
Nemetschek Q3 Design revenue missed, with no clear Q4 steer. GIR expects about 8% growth, similar to the Street, which may move lower.

Bouygues: telecom EBITDA pressure in line with guidance but Street expectations were higher. Equans beat and raised guidance. Construction organic growth was about 4%, in line. Colas' bottom-line beat reflects a provision reversal.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Worst day since 2020. SOX multiples are about 50% below the June/July highs.
Largest one-day change since COVID, back near Liberation Day levels.
Second-largest one-day rise ever, behind only Volmageddon.
Funds 36% of 2026 capex and exceeds the $250bn full-year forecast.
Covers 35% of capex, plus $300bn of IG/HY project finance.

risk_factors: Further AI-capex reassessment for 2028+ from regulation and data-centre permitting.
Credit-spread widening through early December as hyperscalers pull 2027 borrowing forward.
Distressed leveraged AI infrastructure credit (CDS implying >60% 5Y default probability).
Regional data-centre moratoriums covering about 45% of planned US expansion.
Mechanical selling from CTA positioning and ETF-led de-risking.
Memory pricing inflection: NAND procurement frozen, DRAM price rises slowing, 4Q26-1Q27 a critical test.
Middle East situation weighing on Amadeus guidance.
vol_and_positioning: Vol exploded. Hedge monetization dominated early flows in S&P, Nasdaq and VIX. NDX and SPX fixed-strike vols were bid aggressively, most in the front end, and skew steepened dramatically.
VIX vol had its second-largest one-day move higher ever. The GS Vol Panic Index (1m S&P implied vol, VIX vol, 1m skew, term structure slope) reached 9.3 out of 10 intraday.
Flows: GS customer bought 22k SPY 27Nov 700/730 put spreads. VIX calls and call spreads were unwound as VIX spiked above 26.
Implied move through the next day is 1.43%. The straddle through the end of the week was 91bps at the prior close.
High Beta Momentum fell 6.2%, now 51% off the June highs, the worst drawdown in more than 10 years. ETFs were 32% of tape volume, the largest share since June.
Futures closed below the medium-term CTA threshold (7549). Estimated S&P selling over the next week is $7.48bn in a -2.5 stdev scenario.
Asset managers were net sellers, hedge fund flows were about balanced with aggressive toggling of short books, and there was no offsetting bid for hyperscalers and defensive tech.
Global fundamental L/S managers fell 1.3% (a -2 stdev move) and TMT funds fell more than 4%.
geopolitical: Post-election concerns over tighter AI regulation and data-centre permitting after the Democratic midterm sweep.
Regional data-centre moratoriums threaten about 45% of planned US expansion, mainly in Texas.
Middle East situation cited as the reason Amadeus guides to the lower end of its range.

Amadeus's guidance and the Amazon, Uber and DoorDash competitive moves are the only company-specific political or trade items cited; US midterm outcomes are not expected to structurally change long-term federal AI policy.

tension_points.bull_case: Bottom-up demand indicators remain firm, AI-server orders are described as strong by Taiwan supply-chain sources, SOX multiples have compressed about 50%, and Lam Research's $25bn buyback may be followed by others.
tension_points.bear_case: Post-election regulation and data-centre permitting risk, regional moratoriums threatening about 45% of planned US expansion, distressed AI infrastructure credit and no offsetting bid for hyperscalers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further widening of credit spreads through early December as hyperscalers pull forward 2027 borrowing, or evidence that delays to GW and capex builds are not yet priced in.

tension_points.bull_case: Governor-elect Hinojosa said currently permitted projects can complete construction, covering essentially all of 2027 and likely well into 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: Newly permitted projects face tax, consumer power price and water conditions, and moratoriums threaten about 45% of planned US expansion.

theme_stances.evidence: not a lot of clear investor consensus around where we land in 2028+
